analysis:
Examined docs/operations/provider-release.md. Head lines 3 and 204-208 are the only changed lines: a date bump and a new sentence saying a pull-request run on a Darkbloom Sandbox that has no Darkbloom cache skips every cache step of .github/actions/provider-release-build and builds cold, and that the release workflows never skip them. This is documentation only. It leaves the release trust model unchanged: tag-gated production, signing secrets confined to build-and-release, and registration through the external platform API. It adds no new endpoint, secret or authorization path, and the rest of the document is unchanged context.

Examined the patch excerpt of scripts/test-provider-ci-workflow.py (test-only). VALIDATE_GIT now discards a restored .git cache unless it is a real directory with no symlinks, no non-sample hooks, and no config setting core.fsmonitor, core.hooksPath or include/includeif. It also adds a CACHE_GATE_STEP so cache steps are skipped on a Darkbloom Sandbox without its cache. This hardens the CI cache-poisoning boundary and is consistent with the documented 'no signing or publication secrets on the qualification runners' posture. It does not touch the provider runtime threat model (TB-002, TB-003, TB-007, T-041), whose at-rest KV cache is unrelated to the CI cache.

Coverage limits: the patch excerpt is truncated (patch_excerpt_complete=false) and no head text was supplied for the script. The real workflow and action files (.github/actions/provider-release-build/action.yml, release-provider.yml) that implement CACHE_GATE and the .git validation were not supplied. Whether they enforce what the tests assert, and whether the new statement in the doc matches them, is unverified. I found no concrete regression in the supplied evidence.
